title: Prescriptions Class Schedule: Emergency Supply Limits
content:
Whether a Kestrel pharmacist may dispense an emergency supply of a prescription when no refill is available and the prescriber cannot be reached depends on the handling class of the Prescriptions record, as does the size and frequency of that supply.

| Handling class | Emergency supply allowed | Largest days supply of one emergency supply | Most emergency supplies per prescription in any rolling 365 days |
|---|---|---|---|
| Non-Controlled Acute Prescription | No | 0 | 0 |
| Non-Controlled Maintenance Prescription | Yes | 14 | 1 |
| Schedule V Controlled Prescription | No | 0 | 0 |
| Schedule III-IV Controlled Prescription | No | 0 | 0 |
| Schedule II Controlled Prescription | No | 0 | 0 |
| Specialty Limited-Distribution Prescription | No | 0 | 0 |

Only the Non-Controlled Maintenance Prescription class shows Yes: one emergency supply of up to 14 days supply per prescription in any rolling 365 days. Every other class shows No and limits of 0.

**Hypothetical reading.** A patient on a Non-Controlled Maintenance Prescription who has not received an emergency supply on that prescription in the last 365 days is within the class's limit of 1; a Schedule V Controlled Prescription shows No, so the class carries no emergency supply at all.
